title: School Refusal and Childhood Anxiety
diagnosis: Generalized Anxiety Disorder (child) with school refusal
source: U-Word Psychiatry v02 concepts (Immersa rewrite) — anchor for Uber U09
should_avoid: Dismiss somatic complaints without medical rule-out

rationale.GAD-7 / anxiety screening (child-appropr: Quantify worry severity and track response — use developmentally appropriate anxiety screen alongside clinical interview.
rationale.TSH / basic metabolic panel: Morning stomachaches and restlessness can reflect hyperthyroidism or anemia — rule out medical drivers before anchoring on anxiety.
rationale.CBT / psychotherapy referral: First-line for pediatric GAD — exposure for school refusal, cognitive restructuring for catastrophizing about peer judgment.
rationale.School psychologist / 504 coordination: School refusal needs coordinated return-to-school plan, accommodations, and teacher communication — not home isolation.
rationale.SSRI consideration (sertraline / fluoxet: Stepped care when psychotherapy alone is insufficient — sertraline or fluoxetine are first-line SSRIs for child GAD; monitor activation and suicidality early.
rationale.Sleep hygiene / nightmare screen: Sleep-onset worry and bad dreams perpetuate daytime irritability and concentration problems — screen for nightmare disorder and coach sleep routine.
rationale.Safety assessment: No acute suicidal ideation reported, but document safety, protective factors, and family psychiatric history — mother with depression raises genetic and modeling risk.
rationale.Benzodiazepine long-term without psychot: Avoid chronic benzos in children — dependence, cognitive effects, and no exposure work for school refusal.
rationale.Dismiss somatic complaints without medic: Functional abdominal pain is common in child anxiety, but TSH and basic labs still belong in the workup.

hpi: Maya Chen is a 9-year-old girl brought by her mother for worsening school refusal. Three weeks ago a classmate laughed when her pencil rolled off the desk; since then she believes everyone will laugh at her if she returns. She develops nausea and epigastric "stomachaches" on school mornings and cries at the door. At night she lies awake checking that the front-door lock is secure and worries someone could break in. She fidgets during homework and loses track of instructions — her teacher wonders about attention problems, but symptoms track with worry rather than classic hyperactivity. Mother reports lifelong "nervous temperament" and takes medication for depression. No fever, weight loss, tremor, or suicidal statements; she denies wanting to die but says she "can't face school anymore."
hpi_narrative:
Maya Chen is a 9-year-old girl brought by her mother for worsening school refusal. Three weeks ago a classmate laughed when her pencil rolled off the desk; since then she believes everyone will laugh at her if she returns. She develops nausea and epigastric "stomachaches" on school mornings and cries at the door. At night she lies awake checking that the front-door lock is secure and worries someone could break in. She fidgets during homework and loses track of instructions — her teacher wonders about attention problems, but symptoms track with worry rather than classic hyperactivity. Mother reports lifelong "nervous temperament" and takes medication for depression. No fever, weight loss, tremor, or suicidal statements; she denies wanting to die but says she "can't face school anymore."

Mechanism: pervasive anticipatory anxiety drives autonomic arousal (morning GI symptoms), avoidance (refusal), and hypervigilance at sleep onset. Inattention here is likely worry-related — distinguish from ADHD by onset after stressor, situational focus, and improvement when anxiety treated.

Workup: child-appropriate anxiety screen, TSH and basic labs, safety assessment with parent collateral. Treatment: CBT with graded school exposure, school psych coordination, sleep hygiene; consider SSRI if moderate-severe or partial CBT response.

Alert, cooperative with parent present; worried mood, normal thought content, no hallucinations; denies SI/HI today

chief_complaint: Morning stomachaches, school refusal, constant worry about peers laughing
case_summary: Nine-year-old with school refusal after peer embarrassment, pervasive worry, sleep-onset security checking, and worry-related inattention. Pediatric GAD with somatic cues — rule out medical causes, coordinate school return, CBT first-line, SSRI if needed.
